description: The vocabulary of the object a finished run hands back, in all five languages. This library is meant to be used BESIDE the generator, so a reader following an example written in another language should not have to translate the method names. Each language spells the name its own way — camelCase, snake_case, PascalCase — and means exactly the same thing. Older names that predate this table are kept working and are listed under 'also'. Nothing here is deprecated; the point is that ONE of the spellings is the same idea everywhere.
why: There was no guard on this surface, and it drifted: Python had no to_string, Java had no toArray, C# had neither GetAt nor Iterate, Rust had neither to_array nor get_at. Each was reasonable in its own language and wrong for a reader crossing between them.

everyReaderKeepsEachAssert.description: A failing <assert each=> stops every way of reading the run, not only the text. toArray, toColumns, iterate and getAt used to hand back the rows that failed it without a word in four of the five: that= was checked while the run was prepared, each= only in the loop that writes text. A config that looked verified, read the way test code reads it, verified nothing. Each reader refuses with the same message as the text. getAt is asked for the row that fails: it checks the row it hands back, and Rust, which builds the whole run when the object is created, refuses at creation instead.
everyReaderKeepsEachAssert.config: <tdc><env count="3" seed="s"><sequence name="N"><gen type="increment" value="1"/></sequence><assert each="N < 3" says="N stays below three"/></env><block><line><data>${{N}}</data></line></block></tdc>
everyReaderKeepsEachAssert.message: assert failed on row 3: N stays below three
